title: Parallax Background Layers
author: hugejew
selftext: How are people getting parallax background layers to work? Specifically for me in a 2d sidescroller. Are there any tools or approaches people might share to help achieve a 3-layer parallax with proper elements and transparency? The usual suspects image gen web tools have trouble with transparency and making images to be used as layers in this way. I'm using Godot as the engine.

comments.author: Nearby_Ad_3037
comments.body:
I use unity I feel like it’s better but almost similar there is a Z axis and layers which you can layer your background to make a nice scene, and if you are asking how to do it is that you generate your assets individually and organize them same way and you will get a scene like this and there is a parallax button actually to add in unity

https://preview.redd.it/68nlohpbo1sg1.png?width=2188&format=png&auto=webp&s=59863f4b7ab24e4ef9568fb86dddcd7fb8ec1d9f

replies.author: hugejew
replies.body: I saw your post earlier; that scene looks really nice. I'm totally green on game dev. This is my first effort here and I've been at it solidly two months. I can definitely get layers to slide past one another  and parallax effectively, but I'm thinking more on the asset gen side. I haven't found good tooling for asset generation even just for placeholders. I'm ultimately using free asset packs as placeholders to just get the parallax effect working and test it a bit. Ultimately I intend to work with (and pay) a proper artist for this but I'd like to have a solid grounding enough to understand how it even should work and have a better vision for the final product.

replies.author: Nearby_Ad_3037
replies.body:
Awesome man same here once I get the demo out I’m trying to get an artist to replace everything but here is my workflow regarding art generation for this scene and the rest there is  short term and long one so to start 

Easy one, is that I emailed adobe explain to them on a solo developer, and I showed them chapter one of my ￼ they were really really nice and they really like the story so they gave me free access to all their apps in adobe cloud, and to be honest I only used one ☝️ and it’s photoshop in there you can layer all you assets there is a object selection tool and you cut the assets you want individually and it automatically put it in a transparent png which then you can put in unity add all the physics and… 

Now for the other one which is a bit harder, but it’s so much easier in the long-term and more consistent is to train a Lora and build your own workflow inside comfy UI, so you give it let’s say the same images that you did from Photoshop, which all have a transparent background and keep feeding your Lora to teach it how to generate your assets then you install comfy ui and build a workflow with control nodes plenty of YouTube videos on building ones, and boom you are done give it the prompt of the assets houses, castle… and it makes it with the same art you have been feeding it ￼￼￼

replies.author: hugejew
replies.body:
Thanks a lot for the replies. Yeah I think the LoRA method seems to be important as I start to take this seriously. Thanks for the tip on Adobe too.

I'm a little stuck on like, chicken-and-egg tho. I need assets in order to train stable diffusion in order to generate assets. Would it make sense to invest in a few assets up front that I really like, try to maybe generate a few more based on those, then use that to train a LoRA so I can get a similar style and some production-ready stuff?

replies.author: Nearby_Ad_3037
replies.body:
U welcome dude, and for that no I wouldn’t suggest it at all save your money later when you need it not now for training, what I would do I would download a base model with the art you want or download a public use pictures of the art you want to train your Lora, on google there is a lot of free art pics to use that people want to give them without copyright, and that would be your first Lora and then use it generate the actual style and art you want to make your ultimate Lora and here is free Lora’s and models you can use by other people: 

https://civitai.com/models/10346/no-one-read-description-46-9mb-loras
 
Use it to get the style you want to make your Lora

Good luck brother

replies.body: Great resource - thanks a lot for that. It seems like I could start with a LoRA from here and a model either of my own making or from here and use it to learn how to hone in ComfyUI at least, then go from there. Appreciate it!
